CausalChain: RMDN1 upregulation -> Recruitment of HDACs (and coordinated interaction with NSD1/KDM3A) -> Reduced chromatin accessibility -> Suppression of oncogenic transcription -> Improved liver neoplasm prognosis  // Conversely: RMDN1 downregulation -> Reduced HDAC recruitment & increased chromatin activators binding -> Activation of pro-metastatic and angiogenic pathways -> Poorer prognosis
Hypothesis: We hypothesize that RMDN1 acts as a context-dependent epigenetic scaffold in liver neoplasms. When RMDN1 is upregulated, it preferentially recruits HDACs and engages with chromatin modifiers NSD1 and KDM3A, promoting a repressive chromatin state that limits oncogenic transcription and suppresses tumor progression. In contrast, downregulation of RMDN1 diminishes its ability to recruit these repressive complexes, facilitating the binding and activation of chromatin activators that drive pro-metastatic and angiogenic pathways. Our approach will leverage advanced technologies, including CRISPR-mediated epigenetic editing, single-cell ATAC-seq combined with spatial transcriptomics to capture chromatin dynamics, and quantitative proteomics to map alterations in the RMDN1 interactome, thereby providing mechanistic insights and validating the dualistic model of RMDN1 function in liver neoplasms.
Abstract: In liver neoplasms, we propose that RMDN1 functions as a context-dependent epigenetic scaffold that differentially controls chromatin architecture and downstream oncogenic signaling. Specifically, in its upregulated state, RMDN1 recruits histone deacetylases (HDACs) and cooperates with chromatin modifiers such as NSD1 and KDM3A to enforce a compact chromatin configuration that limits oncogenic transcription. Conversely, when RMDN1 is downregulated, the failure to engage HDACs allows chromatin activators to access DNA, thereby promoting pro-metastatic and angiogenic gene expression and, ultimately, a poorer prognosis. This dualistic behavior will be interrogated using precise CRISPR-based epigenetic modifications, single-cell ATAC-seq integrated with spatial transcriptomics, and quantitative high-resolution proteomics to characterize context-dependent shifts in the RMDN1 interactome.
Orignal_vs_New: The revised hypothesis retains the original dualistic model where RMDN1 upregulation leads to HDAC recruitment and chromatin compaction while its downregulation results in a more permissive chromatin state. However, the refined version explicitly incorporates additional chromatin modifiers (NSD1 and KDM3A) into the mechanistic framework, addresses how these interactions may further modulate oncogenic signaling, and clarifies the context dependency. Additionally, it leverages contemporary technological advancements such as CRISPR-driven epigenetic modifications, single-cell ATAC-seq integrated with spatial transcriptomics, and high-resolution quantitative proteomics to enhance practical implementability and provide deeper mechanistic insights.
